patterns.what_worked: Making the NAME the key and the id only a confirmation (one helper: the confirmed id whose own client-resolved name is the expected name) is what makes 'a wrong id degrades to unknown' provable rather than asserted: a wrong id makes the client answer a different spell's name, so the latch stays unknown and the archived seal input stands. Re-reading the tree before writing showed the SoD hard-wait render was ALREADY in nextaction_ui.lua, so that file needed no change - and the one defensive edit I tried was reverted because the engine only publishes the wait together with a hold (dead code, no killable pin). Seven mutations on a /tmp/opencode copy killed every new pin.
patterns.what_was_hard: The client API shape for a name-anchored id is not knowable offline: the classic global and C_Spell differ per family, and the id->name direction is the one that answers on the classic path. Anchoring on the client-resolved name of the id (not on a name->id lookup) keeps the discipline working on the client where the spell exists and inert everywhere else. The anchors are English, so a localized client stays unknown until its names are added - a deliberate, documented limit, not an oversight.
patterns.skill_gap: The offline harness cannot prove the 1.60.x GetSpellInfo for 1311703 / 1311704 / 10333, so the ids stay web-confirmed and client-unconfirmed; the operator's session is the only closure. The runtime-diag reader for the new counter lives in main.lua, which this lane does not own.
